his_line: Non Nobis Oblige ☧ Μὴ ἡμῖν, Κύριε ☧ לֹא לָנוּ יְהוָה ☧
his_line_source: Stefano Theofanous, 2026-10-12, exactly as written (the separators are drawn as the Chi Rho)
hebrew: לֹא לָנוּ יְהוָה לֹא לָנוּ כִּי־לְשִׁמְךָ תֵּן כָּבוֹד עַל־חַסְדְּךָ עַל־אֲמִתֶּךָ׃
hebrew_source: Westminster Leningrad Codex (UXLC 2.5), Ps 115:1, cantillation marks removed; checked against Ginsburg 1894 p. 1300
greek: μὴ ἡμῖν, Κύριε, μὴ ἡμῖν, ἀλλ' ἢ τῷ ὀνόματί σου δὸς δόξαν ἐπὶ τῷ ἐλέει σου καὶ τῇ ἀληθείᾳ σου.
greek_source: Swete, The Old Testament in Greek II (Cambridge 1896), p. 370, Ps 113:9
latin: Non nobis Domine, non nobis: sed nomini tuo da gloriam.
latin_source: Clementine Vulgate, editio princeps (Rome 1592), p. 514, Ps 113:9 (modern spelling of the long s only)
kjv: Not unto us, O LORD, not unto us, but unto thy name give glory, for thy mercy, and for thy truth's sake.
verified_by: Each language checked against the edition named in its source field, 2026-10-12
